cards.title: SUDO SU
cards.description_long: The 'sudo su' command allows a user with sudo privileges to switch to the root user. This gives full administrative control over the system.

main_commands.explanation: Switch to root user, prompt for your password
Switch to root and load root’s environment
Switch to another user with root privileges
Run a single command as root and exit
Open an interactive root shell (similar to sudo su -)

activity: Switch to root with full environment
Switch to another user using sudo su
Run a single command as root

cards.title: SUDO
cards.description_long: The 'sudo' command allows a permitted user to execute a command as the superuser or another user. It is safer than logging in as root directly.

main_commands.explanation: Run update command as root
Restart a service with sudo
List commands you are allowed to run with sudo
Repeat the last command with sudo
Run mkdir as root without switching shell

activity: Run a command as root without switching shell

cards.title: PASSWD
cards.description_long: The 'passwd' command allows you to change your own password or, with sudo, another user's password. It enforces password policies like minimum length and expiration.

main_commands.explanation: Change your own password
Change password for user alice
Lock a user account
Unlock a user account
Force a user to change password at next login

activity: Change another user's password with sudo
Force password change on next login

cards.title: ADDUSER
cards.description_long: The 'adduser' command creates a new user with home directory and initial settings. It is simpler than 'useradd' and includes prompts for setting password and info.

main_commands.explanation: Create a new user bob with home directory
Add user bob and assign to sudo group
Create user without setting password
Create user without prompting for info
Specify default shell for new user

activity: Create a new user with home directory
Create user without extra info prompts
Set custom shell for new user

cards.title: ADDGROUP
cards.description_long: The 'addgroup' command creates a new group. It is useful for managing permissions and access control for multiple users.

main_commands.explanation: Create a new group named developers
Create a group with specific GID
Add an existing user to a new group (depends on distro)
Create a system group
Verify group exists and list its members

activity: Create a group with specific GID
